title: Advocacy groups accuse Trump administration of fast-tracking migrant children's asylum cases
summary:
The groups have filed suit over the handing of children's immigration cases.
Immigrant advocacy groups representing migrant children have sued the Trump administration to stop what they call a "cruel and unlawful scheme" to fast-track migrant children's asylum cases.
In a complaint filed Thursday night, the groups allege that new government policies have transformed the asylum process for migrant children into a "deportation assembly line depriving them of their rights."
The suit comes two days after the Department of Homeland Security announced it was offering unaccompanied migrant children $3,000 to self-deport, a $500 increase over last year's incentive.
Immigration advocacy groups have raised concerns about the initiative, arguing that the same government seeking to deport the minors should not be representing them in court.

title: Trump ramps up third-country US deportations despite global rights outcry
summary:
Third-country deportations, as the practice is known, have been criticised by the US as well as global rights groups like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, as well as the UN.
Those being sent to other countries, rights groups say, would not have been deported without their consent.
A closer look at the third-country deportationsRights groups have tried to tally forcible third-country deportations, and according to the nonprofits Refugees International and Human Rights First, more than 25,000 people have been subject to forcible third-country deportations so far, based on media reports and information from attorneys.
The Department of Homeland Security’s own data includes more than 16,000 cases of third-country deportations since Trump came into office in January 2025 and August 2026, the latest month for which data is available.

title: Want to Self-Sponsor Your U.S. Visa? Avoid These 3 Common Governance Mistakes
summary:

Draft compliant bylaws and employment contractsA common mistake made by early-stage founders looking to self-sponsor is setting up an independent board on paper but leaving corporate bylaws unchanged.
Your bylaws, board charters and executive employment agreement must explicitly delegate executive oversight and firing authority to the board.
Establish governance at entity formationRestructuring your board or altering your bylaws shortly before filing a visa application can raise red flags.

title: Mexican court closes case against official over 2023 detention centre fire
summary:
A Mexican judge has closed the case against Francisco Garduno, former head of the country’s immigration agency, for crimes related to the 2023 fire at a Ciudad Juarez detention centre that killed 40 migrants and injured 30 others.
The incident was the deadliest event ever to occur at a Mexican immigration centre, and critics said it exposed the shortcomings and irregularities in the country’s detention system.
On Tuesday, Judge Victor Manlio Hernandez Calderon ruled that Garduno had fulfilled the court-mandated measures required to address the damage.
The victims have also compared the judge’s decision to close the criminal case to a de facto exoneration for Garduno.
